title: HTTP client in Python with urllib.request
when: A Python script must call an HTTP API or download a file using only the standard library.
prompt:
Goal: A small client that sets timeouts and headers, handles HTTP and network errors, decodes JSON safely and retries politely.
Steps:
1. Build urllib.request.Request(url, data=body, headers={"Accept": "application/json", "User-Agent": "tool/1.0"}, method="POST").
2. Query strings with urllib.parse.urlencode; JSON bodies with json.dumps(payload).encode("utf-8") plus Content-Type: application/json.
3. Always urlopen(req, timeout=10) in a with block.
4. Catch HTTPError first (it has .code and .read()), then URLError, then TimeoutError; raise one ApiError with URL, status and reason.
5. Decode with resp.headers.get_content_charset() or utf-8, then json.loads inside try.
6. Retry GET on URLError, 429 and 5xx up to 3 times (1, 2, 4 s), honoring Retry-After; stream downloads with shutil.copyfileobj to a .part file, then rename.
Quality bar:
- No call can hang forever.
- Errors name the URL, status and a short reason.
- Tokens come from environment variables.
Pitfalls:
- Catching URLError before HTTPError (HTTPError is its subclass).
- Disabling certificate checks to silence an error.
- Reading a large download fully into memory.
Verify:
- [ ] Every urlopen has a timeout.
- [ ] HTTPError and URLError handled.
- [ ] No bare except.
- [ ] Main guard present.
Output: client.py with request helpers and a main() showing one call.

examples.input: python script that fetches exchange rates from an API daily
examples.output: client.py get_json(url) with timeout 10, HTTPError/URLError handling, 3 retries
